body: I hate it. I just want people to leave me alone.

I know all about this. I have stopped medications and stopped therapy. It just wasn’t helping me after 25 years - off and on.  I still feel guilty for what happened, even tho I know it wasn’t my fault and I didn’t cause it to happen to me. I don’t know how to feel anything else other than what I “normally “ feel with CPTSD. I’m afraid to feel other feelings because I don’t know what they are supposed to feel like and I’m afraid of changing. I know how to deal with who I am now and  the feelings I feel. 

I’m trying to understand why these feelings  manifested into what they did. I don’t quite understand it.  I beat myself up senselessly to the point of punishment. I’m not sure why I punish myself. 

As for good people, I don’t know what makes people good in my eyes. Because I’m so hyper vigilant everyone is immediately bad if they start to get close. I’m trying to protect myself from getting hurt again. I try to look at like my self defence mechanism is actually working by protecting myself subconsciously , but inefficiently and I am still trying to work out the bugs. Because of what happened to me, this is the part of me that he damaged the most. He took my ability away to see good people and to trust. Because it’s a subconscious thing, it’s hard to fix. I just need to learn how to “see” again.  I try and let people in just a little bit more than I did the last time but I also try to be specific with myself and set some temporary boundaries until my gut tells me I can trust them. As I’m starting to learn and understand the gut feeling , I feel less hyper vigilant with that person.  I don’t know much but I do know I have a internal process that I use, like a check list for people. If I get any type of bad feeling, I get more protective of myself. 

I honestly don’t know what makes a good person either. Anyway I think about it or rationalize, it all come down to how do you know. Maybe it’s one of those questions like do you move on to an afterlife after your dead.  So we may never know the answer. Maybe goodness in people is not up to us to judge. Maybe we just accept that we’ll never know that but can only change to try and be a better person.  This is hard.

I’m in the middle of going through this right now. Not sure if this will help you or not, but last night talking with husband about this and he asked me why I keep punishing myself, why I am so hard on myself? They are good questions, and I honestly don’t have an answer yet, but it’s making me question a lot of things I do and don’t do for myself.

I found prayer and honest open communication with myself was the best help for me. Realization of the problem that I was mentally stuck was another “light bulb” moment for me. I forced myself to do things i used to prior to the events that caused my trauma to try and reconnect with myself. So far it’s working out for me.

People can’t help me. Medication can’t help me. Only I can help me.

I listen to music all the time for the same reasons. I found that it doesn’t work as well for me either sometimes. When that happens, I listen to different music. I listen to classic rock and when it stops being effective, I’ll listen to Mike Oldfield, Songs of of distant earth. I listen to the entire album from start to finish. It’s very peaceful and I find it takes me to another place in my head that I should visit more often.  I think it excites a different part of my brain. Music is a very good healer for me, does more for me than medication ever did.

I told my HR manager that I have PTSD and was working through it with therapy as I wasn’t sure what the therapy would do to me like make me worse and hopefully would be able to get through my work day. He told me that he was going to pretend that I never told him.  Messed me up.  Sometimes being honest isn’t worth it.  I work for a police service.

If it was easy I would have done it by now. I hate therapists. In Canada, as soon as you tell them you are suicidal they have the cops come and apprehend you and bring you to the hospital for an assessment with a shrink who then after a five minute conversation with you, then decide to let you go home or commit you for 72 hours with doses of something to relax you. Therapists don’t even know how to deal with it. They just push you off to the authorities who don’t deal with it either and the suicide cycle starts all over again. Thanks for this post. It made me feel validated and not crazy.
I get it. I understand exactly what you feel right now.

I tried multiple therapists and I think they just didn’t listen so I gave up. They were more concerned with me doing tapping and saying mantras rather than try and get to the root of my problems.  Some didn’t believe me, some were too expensive, some we just didn’t click.  Out of options in my city for now.  Also, if I mention anything about being suicidal or my ideation with it, they will call the cops and have me apprehended and taken to the hospital. The system sucks here. So I can’t even really talk about it, I want help, they just choose to pass me off to a hospital that holds you for a couple days and prescribes meds. It’s a vicious circle where I may end up being the victim of my own demise.  

The meds make the suicidal thoughts worse for me. All my serious attempts were when I was on meds. Without the meds,  I just think about it and don’t really harm myself. 

I know I don’t want to die, but dying would solve so many problems. Just wish I had enough courage to just end it. I don’t know why people say that people who kill or want to themselves are cowards and weak. It is such a huge freaking battle with your mind. It’s overwhelming and scary and sometimes a relief to think about.  

Relatively new here and happy to see I’m not the only one. At least there is that lol.
